subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this product-wide v1 localization contract, including the proposed Gateway metadata, recipient-locale ownership model, and 21-locale coverage/release commitments?
rationale: The RFC creates cross-surface compatibility and governance commitments that cannot be safely selected by automated review; its own text identifies several owner decisions still needed before implementation.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded v1 RFC
options.body: Approve a reduced contract with named owners for Gateway compatibility, safety copy, locale resolution, and an explicitly staged coverage target.

options.title: Request a narrower design
options.body: Keep the RFC open but limit it to locale resolution and one first implementation surface before adopting product-wide coverage and metadata contracts.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Pause this RFC until core owners choose whether product-wide localization is a current priority and can staff the required safety and language-review roles.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded v1 RFC
recommendation.body: Approve a reduced contract with named owners for Gateway compatibility, safety copy, locale resolution, and an explicitly staged coverage target.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal author can clarify and revise the design in response to the final maintainer direction, though acceptance remains a project-level decision.
